column2: The spokes with yellow and red, the dark ones; the rim with red; the lines outside are white, dark, ruddy, black and yellow.
Thus there are sixteen compartments; so is another mandala; in twelve and six portions thirty-six squares; the lotus, the lane.
White is made of rice flour and the like; red of safflower and the like; yellow with turmeric; black from burnt grain.
One row for the east; the door-ornaments and so on as before; a lotus of twelve finger-breadths in a one-cubit mandala.
Dark with shami leaves and the like; by a hundred thousand repetitions of seed-syllables; with four hundred thousand of mantras; a hundred thousand accomplishes knowledges.
In a two-cubit one it is one cubit; by increase or by the door one may proceed; the seat is four-sided, without rays; the wheel-lotus.
Ten thousand for the intellect-knowledges and a thousand for hymns of praise; first, by a hundred thousand, the purification of the mantra and of oneself.
Half the lotus is said to be of nine; the navel is remembered as three; with eight make the doors; the rim with four finger-breadths.
Likewise, with another hundred thousand, the mantra becomes made a field; first the incomparable oblation of the seed-syllables is declared.
Dividing the field in three, one should mark the inside with two; for the success of the five final vowels, striking on them, one should draw the spokes.
The preliminary service with a tenth part is declared for mantras and the rest; in the higher practice of a mantra one should observe a monthly vow.
One should draw them shaped like blue lotus petals or like citron, or lotus-leaf-wide, as desired.
One should set the left foot on the ground and not accept gifts; thus with two or three times, the middle and highest accomplishments.
Having turned it outside at the rim, standing between the lower junctions, one should turn the root of the spoke, stationed in the middle of the junction.
I shall tell the meditation on mantra by which the fruit born of mantra occurs: the gross, sound-made form is held the outer body.
Standing in the middle of the spoke, one should turn the churning-stick evenly; thus the accomplishments are properly, like citron, even.
The subtle, light-made form is of the heart, made of thought; what is free of thought is declared the supreme.
Dividing the field in seven, fourteen cubits even; divided in two, here a hundred and ninety-six more.
The gross form is mainly that of Varaha, Narasimha and the Shaktis; the form free of thought is declared that of Vasudeva.
With four compartments, in the middle one should draw an auspicious square; all around leave a lane; likewise in the directions one should draw.
The form of the others is remembered as of the heart, always made of thought; the gross is called Vairaja; the subtle becomes the marked.
Again, around the lane, having cleaned the lotuses, in the middle compartment two and two for the neck should be erased in the directions.
The form free of thought is declared the Lordly; the consciousness dwelling in the lotus of the heart, the imperishable light.
Four outside, afterward three and three should be erased; at the sides of the neck one outside — that is called ornament.
One should meditate on the seed as made of seed, in the form of a kadamba flower, like a lamp inside a pot with its emission blocked.
Having cleaned the outer corners, one should wipe seven and inside three; the mandala should be of nine parts; one should worship Hari in the nine-fold array.
Compact and alone, thus the lord of the mantra stays in the heart; in a pot with many holes, rays of just that measure.
A mandala of twenty-five arrays going to the universal form; a field of thirty-two cubits divided by thirty-two evenly.
Thus the seed-rays spread out through channels; then shining, taking the divine body as their own, they stand.
When thus done, a thousand and twenty-four compartments are indicated, with sixteen compartments in the middle.
The channels set out from the heart are within the range of sight; of them the two, of the nature of fire and moon, stand at the nose-tip.
Having drawn an auspicious square, and erased the row at the side, then with sixteen compartments one should draw eight auspicious squares in the directions.
Having mastered the body's breath by the right secret yoga, the mantra-master devoted to repetition and meditation attains the mark of the mantra.
Having again cleaned a row, likewise drawing sixteen auspicious squares, then erasing the row all around one should arrange.

With purified elements and subtle elements, practicing yoga with desire, he obtains anima and the rest; dispassionate, having crossed beyond, in the divine he is freed from mere elements and the grasp of the senses.
Twelve doors in the directions, three and three in order; having erased with six, four in the middle at the sides.
Four inside and two outside, erased for ornament; for the success of the sub-doors, three inside and five outside.
Having cleaned, one should arrange the ornament as before; outside at the corners seven and inside three compartments should be erased.
In the twenty-five-fold array one should worship the supreme Brahman on the lotus; in the middle, from the east on the lotus, Vasudeva and the others in order.
Having worshipped Varaha, then in order on the east lotus, one should worship the arrays until the twenty-sixth.
The whole array as stated in a single lotus in order should be worshipped with effort — Prachetas thinks it a sacrifice.
He thinks the good Achyuta divided by difference of forms. A field of forty cubits one should divide in order further north.
Each in seven again, and likewise one in two again; seven hundred and sixty-four, one thousand.
Of compartments, the auspicious square, and in the middle sixteen compartments; at the side the lane, then eight auspicious squares, then the lane.
Sixteen lotuses, then the lane; a twenty-four-fold lotus; thirty-two lane lotuses, and lane-born in rows.
Then forty with the lane and the remaining three rows; the door-ornaments and sub-ornaments should be after erasing in the middle in the directions.
For success of two, four and six doors one should erase in the four directions; five, three and one outside for success of ornament and sub-door.
Inside at the sides of the doors six, or four in the middle; one should erase two and two; thus the sub-ornaments become six.
In one direction the numbers should be four, by the count.
In each direction there are three doors also; five and five at the corners, in each row in order one should erase. The compartments will thus be so; the auspicious mandala for mortals' worship.
Frightened by the utterance of the names Achyuta, Ananta and Govinda, all diseases perish — I speak the truth, the truth.
Whatever poison, immovable or movable, or artificial, born of teeth, born of nails, born of the sky,
born of spiders and the like, or any other poison that gives pain — may it all be brought to peace; Janardana is praised for him.
Seizing spirits, the corpse-seizers and the Dakini-seizers, Vetalas, Pishachas, Gandharvas, Yakshas and Rakshasas,
Shakuni, Putana and the like, and the Vinayaka seizers, Mukhamandi and the cruel Revati, old Revati,
the fierce seizers called Vriddhaka, and the mother-seizers too — may the deeds of the child Vishnu destroy these child-seizers.
Whatever old seizers there are, and child-seizers anywhere, those burnt by Narasimha's glance, and those even in youth,
may Narasimha, ever of terrible face and great strength, benefactor of the world, make all the seizers utterly nothing.
O Narasimha, great lion, face blazing with garlands of flame, lord of all, devour, devour all seizers, fire-eyed one.
Whatever diseases, great portents, poison, great seizers, whatever cruel beings, and terrible troubles of seizure,
whatever faults in weapon wounds, "flame-donkey" and the like — all those, Janardana, Self of all, Supreme Self,
having assumed some form, O Vasudeva, destroy.
Hurling the Sudarshana discus, most terrible with garlands of flame, bring peace to all evils, O Achyuta, best of gods.
Sudarshana, of great flame, cut, cut, of great sound; let all evil demons go to destruction, O terrible one.
In the east and west, in the south and north, may Narasimha, Self of all, roaring well, make protection.
In heaven, on earth, in the air, behind, at the side, in front, may the revered Janardana of many forms make protection.
As Vishnu is all the world with gods, demons and men, by that truth may the evils of this one be quieted.
As at the remembrance of Vishnu sins at once go to destruction, by that truth may all evil of this one be pacified.
As Vishnu is sung as the Supreme Self in the Vedantas, by that truth may all evil of this one be pacified.
As Vishnu, lord of sacrifice, is sung even among the gods, by that truth may all that I have said be so.
May there be peace and welfare; may this one's evil be pacified. With kusha grass arising from Vasudeva's body, churned by me,
may Govinda, Nara and Narayana wipe it away. So may all sorrows be quieted by repeating Hari.
The wiping-weapon removes all diseases and the like. This is Hari, kusha, Vishnu; diseases are destroyed by me for you.
With two strikings one should meditate on the smoky-colored one marked with a pure moon; one should withdraw mere touch by mere sound through meditation-yoga.
Om Hraum Hah phat Hrum — I withdraw the subtle element of sound, homage. With one striking, one should withdraw space like pure crystal, standing at the tip of the nostrils.
